newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent builds on Monday's gains, eyes on OPEC.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent builds on Monday's gains, eyes on OPEC.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures rose on Tuesday, building on Monday's gains which were prompted by new tension between Iraq and the U.N., traders said.

August Brent was seven cents a barrel firmer at 0929 GMT, trading at $18.05 - negating an important bearish gap on the technical charts between $17.98 and $18.02. July gas oil was $1.25 a tonne up at $161.50.

"It's a little bit of follow-through from yesterday," one broker said. "The physical market is fairly strong too and there is the OPEC meeting which although it is not having too much effect now, it did help a bit of short-covering last night."
Traders of physical North Sea crudes said the market was relatively tight in the short term.

Ministers at this week's OPEC meeting in Vienna were expected to roll over the group's 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) output quota. But dealers said nothing had come out of Vienna so far to have an important impact on the price of oil.

Dealers were still nervous about possible delays to renewed Iraqi exports under the current oil-for-food arrangement with the U.N., following their threats of new sanctions against Iraq over the weekend.
"Whether oil sales will begin by early/mid July is still anybody's guess, and any further delays will certainly support prices," GNI research said in a daily report.

Traders said they also were awaiting the release late on Tuesday of weekly inventory statistics from the U.S. Brokers GNI said they were expecting a weekly draw in crude oil stocks of two or three million barrels,and possibly a slight draw in gasoline inventories.
Technical chart analysts said positive momentum indicators meant prices were likely to rally on Tuesday, with the next target at $18.32.

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives wrote in a daily report: "If we spend too much time above $18.00 it is a clear sign that we have broken the range, therefore any sign of a recovery in the U.S. might also prompt us to cover shorts this afternoon."
